Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'uncommon' (potions.py:877), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy.

Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: Potion.targeted = True (potions.py:878); CombatState.use_potion resolves the enemy with CombatCtx.resolve_target (combat.py:608, 62-66) and the recording's UsePotion carries the 1-based enemy slot (conformance/combat_driver.py:288)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.AnyEnemy is the ONE value the sim's single boolean distinguishes, and `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` confirms `targeted` is True for exactly the five AnyEnemy potions and False for all 46 others. PotionModel.IsValidTarget's AnyEnemy arm (PotionModel.cs:268-271) is `target.Side != Owner.Creature.Side`, and resolve_target only ever returns a member of combat.enemies, so the guard is structurally satisfied. The dead-target arm (`!target.IsAlive` -> false, PotionModel.cs:264-267) is likewise satisfied: resolve_target falls back to the first living enemy when the indexed one is_gone.

CanonicalVars (protected override, Powde.rationale: `new DynamicVar("Demise", 9m)` -- a bare named var rather than a PowerVar, read back as `DynamicVars["Demise"].BaseValue` at PowderedDemise.cs:28. 9, no ascension branch.

OnUse (protected override, PowderedDemis.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<DemisePower>(ctx, target, 9, Owner.Creature, null)` -> `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, target or ctx.enemy, DemisePower, 9, applier=ctx.player)`. Single enemy target, so the AoE-power target-set gap does not arise. DemisePower's own 'lose 9 HP at the end of each of its turns' behaviour is audit/records/power/demise.json's and is not re-verdicted.

guards.issue: CombatManager.cs:889's `!IsExecutingCardOrPotionEffect(player)` is what stops a nested effect from triggering the empty-hand check early, and PotionModel.cs:324-331 is what puts a potion inside that bracket. The sim has no counterpart anywhere. DORMANT for the same reason audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G2 is dormant -- the ported cards that auto-play another card mid-resolution (cards/cascade.py:58, cards/colorless_skills.py:117) do not touch the draw pile between the inner and outer ends -- but recorded separately because the OUTER frame here is a potion, so a fix that brackets only card plays would leave this half open.
